newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan passes telecom bills for NTT restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Japan passes telecom bills for NTT restructuring.

text.p: Japan on Friday changed its telecom laws, including one governing Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), to allow the giant firm to be split up into three units under a single holding company.
Parliament's Upper House passed a revised NTT law paving the way for the telecoms titan to realise its long-held dream of entering the global market through the restructuring.

Under the restructuring, NTT will be split into two regional local carriers and one long-distance group under a holding company. NTT is mapping out details of the restructuring plan and is likely to implement the changes as early as 1999.

Before the revision, the NTT law had stipulated that the company, which is two-thirds owned by the government, must limit its operations to the domestic market. The firm dominates Japan's domestic phone networks, with an 80 percent market share.

The revision of other laws enabled Japan's largest international telecoms firm, Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD), to offer domestic services. It also clarified rules for connecting circuits among telecommunications carriers.
Earlier on Friday, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Hisao Horinouchi welcomed the ongoing "Big Bang" in the nation's fast-growing telecommunications sector.

"The revisions will make it possible for Japan to survive severe competition in the upcoming multimedia era and cope with globalised and borderless telecommunications business," Horinouchi told a news conference.
"I hope NTT will play a leading role in the international and domestic business arenas," he added. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8688
